newsitem.title: ITALY: SOCCER-MILAN LEFT WITH LITTLE HOPE OF EUROPE.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-MILAN LEFT WITH LITTLE HOPE OF EUROPE.

text.p: AC Milan's 2-2 home draw against Lazio on Sunday may well mean the outgoing Italian champions fail to qualify for European competition next season for the first time in a decade.
With two games to play, Milan are ninth on 43 points, five points behind Bologna and Udinese, their main rivals for an UEFA Cup place.
To qualify for Europe, Milan must not only win their remaining two games, away to Vicenza and at home to Cagliari, but also hope that Bologna and Udinese lose their last two.
Four Italian teams qualify for the UEFA Cup and at the moment Internazionale and Lazio seem assured of a place with Sampdoria, Bologna and Udinese battling it out for the other two spots.
Nor will Milan's seemingly impossible task be much facilitated by either Vicenza or Cagliari, two sides with their own pressing needs for points.

Eighth-placed Vicenza are one point ahead of Milan and could themselves theoretically still win a UEFA Cup place while Cagliari are involved in a desperate three-way relegation battle with Piacenza and Perugia.
If Milan miss out on European competition, it will be the first time in a decade that their performance has failed to qualify them.

Milan were absent during the 1991-1992 season but as a result of a ban imposed by UEFA, following Milan's walk out during injury time of a European Cup, quarter-final tie against French side Olympique Marseilles, in protest over failing lights.
Failure to qualify for Europe would round off a thoroughly wretched season for normally all-conquering Milan, winners of five Italian titles and three European Cups since 1988.
